regions.text: ムといふ侍女を寵愛してるた。王が彼女と語るときつねに「ディレラムと云つて含葉を精んだ。彼女はそれに應じてつねに「大君ベエラム」と云つて語を結んだ、かくして押韻の法が起つたといふのである。

quote.translation: According to a Persian legend, a king called Behram dearly loved a serving-woman called Dilara- m. Whenever the king spoke with her he ended his words with "Dilaram", and she in reply always ended hers with "Great lord Behram", and thus, it is said, the art of rhyme arose.

regions.text: 王の名と待女の名とが脚韻を同じくするといふ偶然の一致が基礎となつて押覆の藝術形式が生じたわけである。

quote.translation: The chance coincidence that the king's name and the serving-woman's name shared the same end-rhyme became the basis from which the art form of rhyme arose.

regions.text: ポール・ヴァレリーは一つの語と他の語との間に存する「雙子の徽笑」（souriresjumcaux）といふことを云つてゐるが（alery,Aurore）”語と語との間の音韻上の一致を、雙子相互間の偶然約關係に比較しておるのである。

quote.translation: Paul Valéry speaks of the "twin smiles" (sourires jumeaux) that exist between one word and another (Valéry, Aurore), comparing the phonetic coincidence between word and word to the contingent relation between twins.

regions.text: なほグフレリーは詩を形式約見地から定義して「言語の偶然（運）の純粋なる體系』（Valery,Variee,p159）といひ、また押麗の有する『哲學的の美』（E，アら7）を読いてるる。

quote.translation: Defining poetry from the formal point of view, Valéry further calls it "a pure system of the chances (fortunes) of language" (Valéry, Variété, p. 159), and he speaks of the "philosophical beauty" (Ib., p. 67) that belongs to rhyme.

quote.translation: To take contingency into the form of poetry, as a glance exchanged between sound and sound, a passing-by between word and word, means to symbolise the pulse of life in poetry.
